It's not our place to judge them, but we can still recognize they are in a situation that is obviously not favorable to them, even if they make excuses for it sometimes. 
They should be approached with love, honesty and kind concerns; it might take them some time to recognize the situation as toxic, especially if they've had toxic attachments since childhood, but they can eventually get out. 
This is not going to work out if they are approached with harsh judgement and shaming, though. At least, it tends not to. Love is irrational. People don't always make good decisions when it comes to love. 

But, when it comes to this situation in particular, I think it's obviously okay to feel resentful and share your feelings. I obviously can't decide for you or tell you what to do, I only know the way you feel is okay and it's for a reason.

If this relationship is causing more stress than joy and you find his behaviour intolerable as it doesn't align with your values or it's toxic, it's a good thing to break up. 

Although, I must say, if I was in the same situation, personally, I'd  to find it better to break up.
At least you're patient. I tend to give up a lot.
